result.summary:
Fixes SECURITY-REVIEWER Step 2c's sole BLOCKER (handoffs/WF02-REQ-018/step-02c-security-reviewer.json, S5): apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts's /checkin authorization refusal path wrote no AuditLog row on any of its three refusal branches (no-user / not-staff-for-event / event-ended). Read security-invariants.md S5 in full, apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts and apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts's control flow, and apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaff.ts's addEventStaff/removeEventStaff for the writeAuditLog call-shape precedent, before changing anything.

Fix, per the finding's own suggested alternative ('or in requireEventStaffForEvent itself so every caller of the gate gets it uniformly'): the audit write now lives in domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts's requireEventStaffForEvent (apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts), not duplicated in the handler, so every future caller of this authorization gate gets S5 coverage automatically. The decision logic (actor resolution, action/entity naming, payload shape) is split into a new pure function `buildCheckinRefusalAudit(user, eventId, reason)` so it is unit-testable without a DB, matching this file's own existing `checkEventStaffAuthorization` pattern; `requireEventStaffForEvent` calls it and passes the result plus `evaluationTime` to `writeAuditLog` on every `!result.ok` branch (all three reasons), never on success.

Audit payload shape chosen: `{ actorUserId: user===null ? null : user.id, action: 'checkin.refused', entity: 'event', entityId: eventId, payload: { reason } }` where `reason` is exactly one of CheckInAuthorizationResult's three fixed strings ('no-user' | 'not-staff-for-event' | 'event-ended') -- never free text, never PII (S11). actorUserId is null only for 'no-user' (no User row was ever resolved to attribute the attempt to) and is the resolved internal user.id -- never tg_id -- for the other two reasons. This required widening domain/auditLog.ts's WriteAuditLogInput.actorUserId from `string` to `string | null`, which the schema already supports (db/schema.ts:314, actor_user_id has no notNull()) -- no migration needed, confirming the security finding's own note that no schema blocker exists.

Deliberately did NOT add an audit row on the ok=true (authorized) branch: S5's table requires a log only on the 'scanner is not staff' refusal row; authorization succeeding in this stub is not a status change (S8 scope) and discloses nothing (S3 scope) -- the /checkin stub still performs no check-in write of its own (design section 0.3, unchanged by this rework). Adding a success-path audit row would be inventing a business rule neither S5 nor the design asks for, which core-directives.md forbids -- flagging this reasoning explicitly per the task's own instruction to check invariant text carefully rather than assume.

Tests added: apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts gained a `describe('buildCheckinRefusalAudit', ...)` block with 4 cases -- 'no-user' (actorUserId null), 'not-staff-for-event' and 'event-ended' (actorUserId = resolved user.id, never tg_id), and a dedicated PII/shape-lockdown case asserting the payload carries only the fixed `reason` key and nothing else. This follows the codebase's own established testing boundary (backend_dev_guide.md section 6, and the existing pattern in this very file / eventStaff.test.ts's parseStaffCommandArgs): pure decision logic gets full Vitest coverage; the single DB-write line inside requireEventStaffForEvent itself has no existing DB-mock harness anywhere in this repo (addEventStaff/removeEventStaff's own db.transaction+writeAuditLog calls are likewise not unit-mocked) and was instead independently verified live against a real Postgres per step 6 below, exactly as this rework task specified.

Command output (all run synchronously, real output, no speculation):

$ npm run lint -w apps/bot
> bot@0.1.0 lint
> eslint .
(exit 0, no output -- clean)

$ npm run build
(both apps/web and apps/bot workspaces) -- Next.js build compiled successfully, `tsc -p tsconfig.json` for apps/bot completed with no errors.

$ npx vitest run (root)
 Test Files  10 passed (10)
      Tests  118 passed (118)
(up from 114 passing before this rework -- the 4 new buildCheckinRefusalAudit cases)

Live verification against real Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432; migrations applied via `npx drizzle-kit migrate`): wrote two throwaway Node scripts (apps/bot/verify_checkin_audit*.mjs, run with `node`, deleted afterward -- not committed) that built a real grammY Bot with a stubbed Telegram API transformer (no real token/network needed) wired to the compiled makeCheckInHandler(db) against the real DB, seeded a real chapter+event row, and dispatched real bot.handleUpdate() calls:
  - tg_id with NO User row at all, /checkin <realEventId>: audit_log rows before=1, after=2, delta=+1 exactly. Last row: {action: 'checkin.refused', actorUserId: null, entity: 'event', entityId: <the event's id>, payload: {reason: 'no-user'}}.
  - a registered User (has tg_id, role=member) with NO event_staff row for that event, /checkin <realEventId>: delta=+1 exactly. Last row: {action: 'checkin.refused', actorUserId: <that user's internal id>, entity: 'event', entityId: <the event's id>, payload: {reason: 'not-staff-for-event'}}.
Both confirmed exactly +1 row (never 0, never 2+) with a sensible, PII-free outcome value. The third reason ('event-ended') exercises the identical code path with only isFinished's boolean flipped, already exhaustively covered by the pure-function unit tests above, so a third live run was redundant and was not run. docker compose torn down (`docker compose down -v`) after verification; git status confirmed clean of the scratch scripts before committing.

Files changed: apps/bot/src/domain/auditLog.ts (actorUserId type widened to string | null), apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts (new buildCheckinRefusalAudit export + audit write in requireEventStaffForEvent), apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts (4 new tests). apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts itself is UNCHANGED -- the fix lives entirely in the domain layer per decisions/0004 and per the finding's own preferred alternative, so every current and future caller of requireEventStaffForEvent gets S5 coverage uniformly, not just this one handler.
